page_title: Radif: a YouTube Music app for the Mac

sources.entry: Radif - Unofficial open-source YouTube Music client built with Tauri, with synced lyrics and a video mode, that needs YouTube Music Premium. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/yuvrajangadsingh/radif) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Radif
summary.one_liner: Radif is an unofficial, open-source YouTube Music client for the Mac, with synced lyrics, a notch title peek, and music video playback.
use_cases: Playing YouTube Music on a Mac in a dedicated app
Watching music videos from YouTube Music
Installing a Mac music app via Homebrew
Checking song titles at the notch without opening a window
summary.what_it_does: Radif is an unofficial YouTube Music app for macOS, built with Tauri. It shows synced lyrics for songs and includes a title peek at the MacBook notch. It can play music videos as well as songs. Songs are played through yt-dlp with a local cache. It can be installed with a Homebrew cask command, after which the user signs in with a Google account that has YouTube Music Premium. The source code is public under GPL-3.0.
notable: Synced lyrics and a title peek at the notch
caveats: Requires a YouTube Music Premium account; free accounts won't play songs
Not signed with Apple's paid developer certificate, so macOS may block the first open (Homebrew install clears this flag)
Unofficial and not affiliated with Google or YouTube
